newsitem.title: USA: Edison delays 1,070 MW Calif. nuke restart.
newsitem.headline: Edison delays 1,070 MW Calif. nuke restart.

text.p: Edison International said Wednesday its 1,070 megawatt (MW) San Onofre 2 power plant has developed another small leak and will not restart Thursday, as earlier expected.
Operators discovered "a leak in a plug associated with a valve. We will have to cool down the unit," Edison spokesman Ray Golden said.
The unit was preparing to begin ramping up to full power on Thursday when the leak was discovered.
The leaking plug is associated with a valve within an internal water cooling system inside the plant's nuclear containment building.
"It is a contained system, there was no discharge and no threat to the public," Golden said.
He said the company did not yet know if the unit would need to return to cold shutdown, but it would definitely not be restarting on Thursday.
The unit has been down for refueling since November 30, with its restart postponed several times already by unexpected repair work.
The San Onofre plant is majority owned (75 percent) and operated by Edison, while Enova Corp's San Diego Gas and Electric Co owns 20 percent and the cities of Annaheim and Riverside own 5 percent.
